Subject: Private deploy compatibility: Windows operator stations, air-gapped install & patching workflow

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the RFP response so far — we're working through Section B (on-prem / air-gapped deployability) and need a few clarifications to validate our internal controls and operator workflows. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Private deployments?

1) Operator workstation support: we run a mix of Windows 10 LTSC (2019 baseline) and Windows Server 2019 on operator consoles. Do you support these OS versions for the operator UI client and the on-prem management tools? Any documented limitations?

2) Offline install media & signed images: For air-gapped installs we require signed install artifacts and a checksum verification process we can audit. Describe how images are signed, how checksums are generated/verified, and whether you provide an offline installer bundle with PGP/GPG signatures or equivalent.

3) Registry/artifact mirroring: we plan to mirror container registries into our air-gapped network. Does Redwood provide guidance or tooling for mirroring your runtime/container images and Helm charts? Are private registry URLs stable across minor releases?

4) Patching & OS updates: we need a recommended process for applying vendor patches to operator workstations while preserving the offline posture. Do you offer a documented patching cadence and an offline package distribution method?

5) HSM/KMS integration & key custody: we will require HSM-backed keys for encrypting model artifacts at rest. Does Redwood Private support external HSMs and customer-managed keys? Any constraints for air-gapped KMS bridges?

6) Runbook / operator attestation: as part of our audit we need a short operator runbook excerpt showing the sequence for: bootstrapping a new operator workstation, verifying identities, and performing a safe rollback of a model version. Can you provide a stub we can review?

Can you get answers and any sample artifacts back to us by EOD Apr 20 PST? We're tightening timelines for procurement. I've attached the relevant RFP section (AstraMed-RFP-sectionB.pdf) with inline references.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lopez
Director, Infrastructure Security

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (install/runtime) and Jonas (deploy engineering) to provide the technical artifacts. High level answers up front:

- Operator stations: We support Windows 10 LTSC and Windows Server 2019 for the admin/ops clients. We maintain a lightweight Electron-based operator UI with an option to run in compatibility mode for LTSC images; there are known limitations around older TLS stacks that we document.

- Signed offline bundles: Redwood provides an offline install bundle (tar.gz) per release that includes a signed manifest (SHA-512) and a PGP-signed release certificate. We also publish a detached signature and a TXT checksum file. We'll attach the install guidelines and a compat matrix.

- Registry mirroring: We provide recommended manifests and a registry-mirroring playbook (registry-mirroring-process.docx) and we support stable image tags for patch-level updates — major versions may move tags but we provide a mapping file.

- Patching: We publish a quarterly security patch cadence plus critical emergency patches. For air-gapped customers we provide offline patch bundles and an operator checklist for staged rollouts.

- HSM/KMS: Redwood Private integrates with customer-managed KMS (KMIP/HSMs supported) and can be configured to use a local HSM for model key wrapping. Air-gapped KMS bridges are supported via a proxy appliance; we'll include a reference integration note.

Attached: redwood-offline-install-guidelines.pdf, operator-stations-compat-matrix.xlsx, registry-mirroring-process.docx. Ben/Jonas — can you add the signed-image/checksum details and a short runbook excerpt for Anna by EOD Apr 20 PST?

Best,
Irene

Anna / Irene — adding the technical nitty-gritty requested. Key points below; I've attached a short text artifact that contains the signing chain checklist and a sample signed checksum.

1) Image signing & checksum process:
- Release pipeline produces OCI images and an "offline-bundle" tarball. For air-gapped deliveries we produce a signed bundle with: bundle.tar.gz, bundle.sha512.txt, bundle.sig (PGP detached), and manifest.json (includes image digests).
- PGP keys are maintained in our release KMS; when requested we provision a release signing keypair for the customer to verify OR we generate an offline-verified signing certificate chain and provide the public key.
- Verification: the operator runs sha512sum -c bundle.sha512.txt and then gpg --verify bundle.sig manifest.json. We include a verification script in the bundle.

2) Registry mirroring guidance:
- We supply a mirroring script (rsync + skopeo-based) and a mapping file (image_name -> digest) to pin images. For patch-only updates, we publish a pinned digest list so you don't have to re-sync everything.
- Note: minor release tags are stable for 90 days; long-term pinning should use digests shipped in the manifest.

3) Operator workstation compatibility:
- Windows 10 LTSC (2019 baseline) supported for the operator UI; we recommend enabling TLS 1.2+ and applying vendor updates to the crypto stack.
- Windows Server 2019 supported for headless operator services (service account installations). Windows Server 2022 is supported in preview for upcoming releases.
- Known limitation: older group policy deployments that block RSACNG providers may require local policy changes — documented in the compat matrix.

4) Offline patch distribution:
- We produce delta patch bundles and full patch bundles. The recommended process: mirror new bundle to staging registry -> run verification on staging -> run canary on a small operator group -> full rollout using the operator checklist.

5) HSM integration:
- We support KMIP-compatible HSMs and customer-provided key wrapping keys. In air-gapped scenarios we deploy a small KMS bridge VM that speaks KMIP to the HSM and HTTPS to the Redwood runtime using mutual TLS.

Attachments: signed-image-checksum-process.txt, sbom-quick-sample.json

If helpful I can include example commands and a small demo script for verification during the call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the kind of detail we need. A few follow-ups inline below.

> PGP keys are maintained in our release KMS; when requested we provision a release signing keypair for the customer to verify

Can you clarify whether AstraMed would receive a static public key for verification that we can pin in our image verification policy? We cannot rely on network access to fetch keys.

> minor release tags are stable for 90 days

We will require a deprecation/notification window for tag changes; 90 days is acceptable if you commit to email + portal notice at T-60 and T-14 for any breaking tag changes. Can you confirm communication SLAs?

> HSM integration and KMS bridge VM

A couple security constraints: the bridge VM must not open outbound to the internet and must have an auditable configuration profile. Can you provide an example KMIP client config and the minimum required outbound endpoints (if any) so our networking team can pre-authorize the appliance?

Finally — our procurement team needs sample evidence of the SBOM process and a short runbook excerpt (just 6–8 steps) for: provisioning a new operator workstation, verifying the bundle, and performing a rollback. Can you include those items as separate attachments so we can attach them to the procurement packet?

Matt (cc) — if you need anything from a third-party validation perspective let us know.

Thanks,
Anna

Anna — thanks for the follow-ups. Quick answers and next steps (we can walk these in a 45-minute technical demo next week):

- Static verification key: yes — we can provide a customer-dedicated signing public key (PEM) that you can pin locally. We'll include instructions to install it into the verification tool so no network reachability is required.

- Communication SLA for tag deprecation: Redwood will publish notice to the customer portal and send email at T-60 and T-14 before any tag changes. For AstraMed enterprise customers we also provide a webhook-based notification optional subscription (pull model; you host the webhook endpoint).

- KMIP/KMS bridge networking: the bridge VM requires only outbound access to the HSM on KMIP ports (default 5696) or a direct SAN connection — no internet egress is required. If you run a local HSM we can operate in fully isolated mode. Example KMIP client config snippet (inline):

-----BEGIN RUNBOOK SNIPPET-----
1) Provision operator workstation VM (Windows 10 LTSC) and join target admin OU.
2) Copy offline bundle to local secure staging share (\staging\redwood) and verify checksum: sha512sum -c bundle.sha512.txt
3) Verify signature: gpg --verify bundle.sig manifest.json (using pinned public key.pem)
4) Load images to local registry mirror: skopeo copy --all docker-archive:bundle.tar docker://local-registry.internal/namespace/bundle
5) Perform a canary install on "op-svc-canary" host; validate health-checks + metrics for 30m
6) If canary passes, promote images and scale to operator pool; to rollback, set orchestration target to previous pinned digest and restart operator service
-----END RUNBOOK SNIPPET-----

Attachments we'll provide in a secure share for procurement: customer-verification-publickey.pem, sbom-collection-sample.json, runbook-excerpt.txt, and a short screen-capture demo we can present in the scheduled call.

Proposed demo slots: Apr 23 (10:00–10:45 PDT) or Apr 24 (13:00–13:45 PDT). Let me know which works and we'll send a calendar invite + temporary demo access token. We'll also include a short DocuSign NDA link if you want to accelerate the demo build.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
